solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Russian royal raves about cracking shrimp

indicators.note: 'about' suggests being turned around and jumbled, so the word raves is rearranged
something cracking a shell gets inside it, so the jumbled letters go into the word for shrimp

blocks.note: a titch is a very small person, a shrimp
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian prince is ranting while breaking open a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrimp' looks like seafood, but here it is British slang for a tiny person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarevitch was the son of a Russian tsar, so a member of the imperial family.

clue.text: A little gas released from the rear? …

blocks.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
the rump is the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A small whiff escapes from someone's backside, and the ellipsis promises more wind to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue, which also deals in wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to trump is to fart, a small emission of intestinal wind.

clue.text: … wind the setter’s admitted to just now

indicators.note: being admitted to a place means being let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: soon can mean presently or just now in older usage
the setter says 'I am', contracted to I'M

explanation.surface: Continuing the joke, the setter confesses to having just passed some wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just now' as a meaning of soon is an older usage, still listed in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The simoom or simoon is a hot, dry, dust-laden desert storm blowing across Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Bear on stage acting, Rupert perhaps?

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank
Rupert Brooke, the First World War poet

explanation.surface: A bear appears in a play, and someone wonders whether the actor is Rupert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On stage' marks the word as one used by Shakespeare rather than in everyday speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrooke is a Shakespearean form of brook, meaning to tolerate or endure, so a stage verb for putting up with something.

clue.text: Praying mantis, one involved in awful terror, she’s biting heads off

indicators.note: having their heads off means the first letter of each nearby word is lost
to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it
something awful is a mess, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: one as the indefinite article
the word without its first letter
the word without its first letter, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A female mantis horrifies, devouring males by biting their heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into ERROR, and those letters plus HES are all rearranged together into REARHORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearhorse is an old dialect name for the praying mantis, from the way it rears up like a horse.

clue.text: US jurors exercised nerve in nailing us

indicators.note: something exercised is worked over and moved about, so these letters are rearranged
nailing something down holds it fast inside, so the rearranged letters enclose another piece

blocks.note: seven letters rearranged
in informal British speech 'us' means me, as in 'give us a kiss'

explanation.surface: American jury members steeled themselves to convict the speaker and friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'us' at the end is separate from the 'US' of the definition; the setter plays on the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A venireman is someone summoned for jury service under a writ of venire in American courts.

clue.text: Weaver spinning an item of headgear

indicators.note: spinning turns a thing round, so the phrase is read from its end

blocks.note: an item of headgear is a hat, with the article kept

explanation.surface: Someone at a loom is twirling a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaver' suggests a person at a loom; here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The taha is a South African weaverbird, a species named for its woven hanging nests.

clue.text: Knack of using Maori’s ultimate pit for cooking

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the last letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to get the hang of something is to have the knack of using it
final letter of Maori

explanation.surface: A Maori is skilled at using an earth oven to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangi is a traditional Maori earth oven, a hole lined with hot stones in which food is steamed.

clue.text: Ability once gained from working in engineering

indicators.note: the letters are obtained from inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: inside workING IN Engineering

explanation.surface: A skill learnt on the job in the engineering trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingine is an archaic spelling of engine in its old sense of native wit, talent or genius.

clue.text: Stand for display before crowd’s doubling

indicators.note: doubling back means turning round and going the other way

blocks.note: the gate is the attendance at a sports match
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something is put on show ahead of a crowd that keeps growing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport the gate is the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a piece of furniture with open shelves on which ornaments are shown off.

clue.text: Families having no time for fruit

indicators.note: having none of something means it is left out of the word

blocks.note: tribes are groups of related families
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Busy households have no time to eat fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIBES loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribes is the botanical genus of currants and gooseberries, used here for their berries.

clue.text: Shocking band’s taken aback TV presenter

indicators.note: taken aback, read literally, is carried backwards

blocks.note: a band or strip of tape
Ant McPartlin of the British TV double act Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A musical group is startled by a scandalous TV host.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a long-running presenting duo on British television.
explanation.definitionFit: Épatant is French for startling or flabbergasting, borrowed into English as a word for outrageously striking.

clue.text: Pilgrimage united heading to Mecca with expression of joy

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in football club names
first letter
a cheer, short for hurrah

explanation.surface: Pilgrims travel together to Mecca, cheering as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: The umrah is the lesser Muslim journey to Mecca, which may be made at any time of year.

clue.text: Japanese painting put back in warehouse by afternoon

indicators.note: putting a word back sets it in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a hong is a Chinese warehouse or trading house
A is a dictionary abbreviation for afternoon

explanation.surface: A Japanese picture is returned to storage after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: IN reversed gives NI, followed by HONG and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihonga is a style of Japanese art using traditional materials and techniques, as opposed to Western-style oil works.

clue.text: Sterile chamber reflecting latest in technology

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards
the latest of something is its final part, so only the end letter is used

blocks.note: a chamber is a room
last letter

explanation.surface: A germ-free clean room shows off the newest hi-tech kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sterile' suggests a germ-free lab, but it is the barren-land sense that is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Moory means like moorland, and so barren and unproductive, in the sense of land that yields nothing.

clue.text: Discerning joy with the aged filling each day

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something else, as in a sandwich

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for each
glee is delight
ye is the olde-worlde spelling of the, so an aged 'the'
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Being perceptive brings old people happiness each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The aged' looks like elderly people but means the archaic word for the. GLEE plus YE fills EA and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagle-eyed means sharp-sighted, noticing small details, so perceptive and discriminating.

clue.text: Police arresting hawker?

indicators.note: to police something is to regulate and put it in order, so the following letters get reorganised

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers detain a street seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' reads as the noun doing the arresting, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange. A hawker is usually a pedlar; the question mark points to a keeper of hawks.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringer is a falconer, specifically one who keeps goshawks, so literally a hawker.

clue.text: Rides in a rickety boneshaker?

indicators.note: something rickety is shaky and liable to fall apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rides along on a wobbly old bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The draisine was an early pedal-less two-wheeler pushed along by the feet, a precursor of the bicycle.

clue.text: Breed of cattle beginning to offer cracking joint

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only
something cracking a thing breaks into it, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: the ankle is a joint
first letter

explanation.surface: A cattle breed is being offered just as a joint gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside ANKLE after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankole cattle are a long-horned African breed from Uganda, known for their huge curved horns.

clue.text: Support Amnesty International ball

blocks.note: the organisation's initials
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Backing a human rights charity by holding a fundraising ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidance is an old word for help or assistance, the act of giving aid.

clue.text: Almost nothing on channel down under, it’s a pig

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down entry, one piece written on another sits below it

blocks.note: a gut is a narrow channel or strait
zero is nothing

explanation.surface: An Australian TV channel shows next to nothing worth watching but a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts ZER below GUT. 'Down under' flags Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a gutzer, or gutser, is a greedy person, a glutton who eats like a hog.

clue.text: Pep Guardiola’s back securing a point, one from Roma?

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
securing something holds it fast inside, so a pair of letters is enclosed

blocks.note: pep and zing both mean liveliness
final letter of Guardiola
taken as written
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Manchester City's manager has his defence protect a lead against a team from Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Pep Guardiola is the Manchester City football manager, but 'Pep' is separate wordplay. 'Roma' suggests the Italian club, but means the Romani people.
explanation.definitionFit: A zingana is a female gypsy, from the Italian zingara, so a woman of the Romani people.

clue.text: Bacardi? First two knocked back again

indicators.note: knocked back here means struck off and rejected, so those letters go

blocks.note: Bacardi is a well-known brand of white rum
the first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone downs a couple of Bacardis in a row and orders another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, which fits the rum; it means the opening pair is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterum is Latin for once more, used in English for a repeat instruction or second occasion.

clue.text: Palm oil’s given energy for one beset by stress

indicators.note: something given one thing for another has the first swapped in place of the second
beset by means surrounded on all sides, so this goes inside

blocks.note: to try someone is to strain or stress them
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Palm oil gives a boost to someone under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Both try and stress are verbs here, meaning to put under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: The troely is a South American palm whose huge leaves are used for thatch.

clue.text: Like a gull by the sea, head back a little

indicators.note: the first letter is moved a short way back down the alphabet, one place earlier

blocks.note: marine means of or by the sea

explanation.surface: A gull at the seaside pulls its head back slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: M becomes L, the letter just before it in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Larine means relating to or resembling gulls, from Larus, the Latin genus name for these seabirds.

clue.text: Indonesian retreat inspiring cry of joy

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside the other

blocks.note: a nest is a snug retreat
io is a classical shout of triumph

explanation.surface: A holiday hideaway in Indonesia brings shouts of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indonesian' is read literally: someone from islands, as the -nesia part comes from Greek nesos, island.
explanation.definitionFit: A nesiot is an islander, and an Indonesian lives on one of thousands of islands.

clue.text: Irish sausage made from minced deer shin

indicators.note: minced meat is chopped up and mixed, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sausage from Ireland is made from ground venison leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Drisheen is a black pudding from Cork, a blood sausage traditionally made with sheep's blood.

clue.text: Provided with plans directly after independence

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the one that follows

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent or independence
dead means directly, as in dead ahead

explanation.surface: A newly independent country is given a blueprint straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Idea'd, or idead, is an old adjective for furnished with notions or schemes in the mind.

clue.text: Opening chapter taken from bible, perhaps

indicators.note: something taken from a word is removed from it

blocks.note: the bible is a ruminant's third stomach, so named for its many leaf-like folds
CH is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: The first chapter is removed from a copy of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening chapter' looks like one phrase, but 'Opening' is the definition. A cow's omasum is also called the bible or manyplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a small aperture or pore, as in a plant leaf or a surgically made hole.

clue.text: Fuss about closure of various parts of women’s quarters

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
the closure of a word is its ending, so the last letter

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
last letter

explanation.surface: A fuss over the closing of several sections of the women's rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: ADO reversed gives ODA, then S.
explanation.definitionFit: An oda is a room within a harem, the secluded quarters of a Muslim household's women.

clue.text: Worry US criminal’s inside

indicators.note: only what is inside is wanted, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: a gangster, the classic American mobster

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious that an American crook has got in.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the G from the front of GANGSTER and ER from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of deep anxiety or dread, a state of persistent unease.

clue.text: Year-end turns into this?

indicators.note: turning into something means changing form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The close of one year becomes something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the year's end becomes the first day of the next. Neerday is the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ne'erday is the Scottish name for New Year's Day, which follows straight on from the old year's close.

clue.text: Drama about deity striking a tree

indicators.note: striking out something removes it from the word
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: No, or Noh, is classical Japanese drama
Gaia, the Greek earth goddess
taken as written

explanation.surface: A play about a god hitting a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Noh is the classical masked theatre of Japan, also spelt No.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngaio is a small New Zealand tree with white flowers and edible fruit.

clue.text: Club-shaped key is binned getting corroded

indicators.note: binned means thrown away, so those letters are discarded

blocks.note: clavis is Latin for key, also used in English for a glossary
taken as written
ate, as in rust ate into the metal

explanation.surface: A club-shaped key is thrown out because it has rusted.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAVIS without IS leaves CLAV, then ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clavate is a botanical term for thickening towards the tip, like a cudgel, from Latin clava.

clue.text: Cat trapping tails of mice in spite

indicators.note: tails are the end bits, so the final letter of each word is taken
trapping something holds it inside

blocks.note: in slang to cat is to vomit, shortened to vom
last letters of both words

explanation.surface: A cat catches mice out of sheer malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' looks like the animal, but it is slang for throwing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is bitter malice or hostility, extended from the poison of snakes.

clue.text: Wanted things dried at sea abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters wander

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Items someone longed for have been dried out at sea in foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things needed or desired, from the Latin plural for things longed for.
